page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfc6.4xlarge consistently in the average tier across multiple performance dimensions. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1435.0 and a multi-core score of 15316.01. Memory subsystem tests show a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 853.47 GB/sec, which drops to 87.94 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 37.05 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, the instance handles 15.25 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 12.43 GB/sec.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is structured for compute-bound tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage tier selected. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-only configuration processes a small 135M LLM model at 935.61 prompt tokens per second, but performance drops to a weak 23.1 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. This hardware profile is suited for compute-optimized workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations.
